subject: Materials Science
title: Ion Implantation: Doping with Precision
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Ion Implantation: Doping with Precision.

hook.text: To dope a silicon chip, engineers fire ions into it at 200,000 km/h — embedding atoms one by one.

buildup.text: An ion implanter accelerates dopant atoms — boron or phosphorus — and shoots them into the wafer.

discovery.text: Implant energy controls depth. Dose controls concentration. Together they sculpt the doping profile.

twist.text: Implantation damages the crystal lattice — a high-temperature anneal is needed to heal the silicon.

climax.text: Every transistor on a modern chip relies on ion implantation to place dopants with nanometer accuracy.

punchline.text: Shooting atoms into silicon — that's how chips get their personality.

quiz.question: Why must silicon be annealed after ion implantation?
options: To remove excess dopant atoms from the surface
To heal crystal damage caused by the implanted ions
